name: std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator<T>::allocate_object
intro:
Allocates storage for n objects of type U using the underlying memory resource.

If std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() / sizeof(U) < n, throws std::bad_array_new_length, otherwise equivalent to return static_cast<U*>(allocate_bytes(n * sizeof(U), alignof(U)));.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
n

 -

 the number of objects to allocate storage for

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: A pointer to the allocated storage.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text:
This function was introduced for use with the fully-specialized allocator std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator<>, but it may be useful in any specialization as a shortcut to avoid having to rebind from std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator<T> to std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator<U>.

Since U is not deduced, it must be provided as a template argument when calling this function.

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.text: Throws std::bad_array_new_length if n > std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() / sizeof(U); may also be any exceptions thrown by the call to resource()->allocate.

examples.title: Practical use case
examples.input: Allocate, construct, destroy, and release storage. Public allocate/deallocate/is_equal dispatch to each resource's protected do_* implementation.

summary: Allocates storage for n objects of type U using the underlying memory resource.
